Finds and excavations

State dig in Nagapattinam recovers Chola-period bronzes of Nataraja and Sivakami

Tamil Nadu's archaeology department has found two bronze images, of Nataraja and the goddess Sivakami, about a metre below ground at an excavation in Nagapattinam district. Experts provisionally date them to the 12th century.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 8 November 2026

Where
Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu

Archaeologists of the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology have recovered two bronze images, one of Nataraja and one of the goddess Sivakami, at an excavation in Nagapattinam district. The find was made public on 30 October 2026, when the state's Minister for Tamil Development, A. Rajmohan, shared photographs on X, PTI and DT Next reported. The minister said that "several statues have been discovered", but only these two have been described.

According to DT Next and The Hans India, the Nataraja is a standing, four-armed figure in the Ananda Tandava, the dance of bliss, 110 cm high and 100 cm wide. The Sivakami is a standing, two-armed figure in the tribhanga, or triple-bend, posture, 82 cm high and 23 cm wide. Each was found with its pedestal, about a metre below the surface.

The date is a first estimate. Experts place both images in the 12th century CE, in the late Chola period, from an initial study of their form, iconography, ornament and pedestal style. No scientific analysis of the metal has been reported.

An official quoted by the two papers said the bronzes add to what is known of religious practice, metalworking and the metal sculpture schools centred on Nagapattinam in its era of sea trade under the Cholas.

The excavation began on 3 August and is continuing. The reports do not name the exact site within the district or describe the other statues the minister mentioned.
